family.description: This domain is found in eukaryotic proteins [[cite:PUB00019471]] required for post-translational sulfatase modification (SUMF1). These proteins are associated with the rare disorder multiple sulfatase deficiency (MSD) [[cite:PUB00033658]]. The protein product of the SUMF1 gene is FGE, formylglycine (FGly),-generating enzyme, which is a sulfatase. Sulfatases are enzymes essential for degradation and remodelling of sulfate esters, and formylglycine (FGly), the key catalytic in the active site, is unique to sulfatases [[cite:PUB00038408]]. FGE is localised to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and interacts with and modifies the unfolded form of newly synthesised sulfatases. FGE is a single-domain monomer with a surprising paucity of secondary structure that adopts a unique fold which is stabilised by two Ca2+ ions. The effect of all mutations found in MSD patients is explained by the FGE structure, providing a molecular basis for MSD. A redox-active disulfide bond is present in the active site of FGE. An oxidised cysteine residue, possibly cysteine sulfenic acid, has been detected that may allow formulation of a structure-based mechanism for FGly formation from cysteine residues in all sulfatases [[cite:PUB00055960]]. In Mycobacteria and Treponema denticola this enzyme functions as an iron(II)-dependent oxidoreductase [[cite:PUB00060032],[cite:PUB00066766]]. This domain is also found in the Serine/threonine-protein kinase Pkn1 from Chlamydia trachomatis which is a multidomain protein. Pkn1 plays a role in specific interactions with host proteins during host intracellular growth.
family.name: Sulfatase-modifying factor enzyme 1-like domain
